newsitem.title: GERMANY: Dollar strength boosts German shares to new highs.
newsitem.headline: Dollar strength boosts German shares to new highs.

text.p: German shares soared to new record highs on Tuesday as the highest dollar level against the mark for almost two years boosted the market.

The DAX index of 30 leading shares roared to a new bourse record high of 2,894.64 points, up 36.04 points, or 1.26 percent, with dealers saying the crucial 2,900 point level was now within the reach of the index.
The IBIS DAX, measuring all-day computer dealings in the index, touched an all-time high 2,897.24 points.
"Everybody who was in the market is happy and everybody else is being forced to pile in," said one trader. "Psychogically the DAX is already at 2,900 points."
German government bond strength provided additional support for the market.

The U.S. currency rose above the crucial 1.56 mark level overnight following comments by Bundesbank chief economist Otmar Issing and New York Federal Reserve Bank William McDonough on the dollar becoming more important in the run up to European monetary union.
Dollar strength benefited the German export-oriented chemicals companies in particular.

Shares in BASF AG jumped over four percent, climbing 2.42 marks to 60.43 marks, Bayer AG rose almost three percent, or 1.73 marks to 64.35 marks, while Hoechst gained 90 pfennigs, 1.3 percent, to 69.50 marks.
"The climb in chemicals has been brutal," said one trader.
Shares in automakers, major exporters, also forged ahead, Daimler-Benz AG gaining three percent or 3.10 marks to 105.20 marks and BMW AG up 21 marks at 1,032 marks.
But shares in Europe's largest carmaker Volkswagen missed out on much of the rally, gaining only 3.50 marks to 590.50 marks.

In early electronic IBIS dealings the stock had dropped over three percent to touch 574 marks, after a U.S. judge denied the firm's motion to dismiss General Motors Corp.'s remaining industrial espionage claims against the German carmaker.

Meanwhile preference shares in luxury carmaker Porsche gained twenty marks to 1,210 marks, after the firm said it expected 1996/97 profits to match those in 1995/96 and said first quarter sales rose by 40 percent.
